summary: Addresses the tendency of autoregressive longitudinal electronic health record generators to underrepresent rare diagnosis codes and their co-occurrence structure, by adding a frequency-derived prior bias to the output logits as a temporary training scaffold that is annealed to zero, so the model internalizes rare-event dependencies in its own parameters instead of depending on an external correction at inference, and supports zero-shot adaptation to a population with different code frequencies through a delta-bias correction. CTGAN is present only as a bracket citation in the related work, standing in for the GAN-based tabular generators the longitudinal EHR line has moved past and, in one place, for the conditional tabular generators whose attribute conditioning the paper's zero-shot distribution control is positioned against.
evidence: the introduction states that GAN and VAE-based methods [9, 10] improved privacy-preserving generation but often struggled to preserve longitudinal dependency structure, and the related-work section places [9, 10, 16] as the GAN, VAE and correlation-aware models for discrete or tabular medical records that longitudinal generation progressed from; reference [10] is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni (2019) and [9] is Choi et al. (2017). CTGAN is never named in the body and the compared baselines are LSTM, EVA, SynTEG, a GPT-style model and HALO, so the citation is a grouped one in a sequence-generation paper. Merged from the duplicate curation of arXiv 2607.12645 (correction shard 91). The paper was curated twice, in shard 66 (slice A) and shard 80 (slice C), under the same id and with the same judgment, citation_only importance 1. The shard 66 record was removed and its fuller evidence is carried here. The tight scan returns one hit in the whole PDF, the bibliography entry [10] for Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni; CTGAN is never named in prose. Reference [10] is bracket-cited four times, three of them in grouped lists: the introduction states that GAN and VAE-based methods [9, 10] improved privacy-preserving generation but struggled to preserve longitudinal dependency structure; section 2 states that synthetic EHR generation has progressed from GAN-, VAE- and correlation-aware models for discrete or tabular medical records [9, 10, 16] to temporal simulators; and the same section groups [10, 26-28] as label-shift and controllable-synthesis work that does not address zero-shot control. The fourth is the closest to individuated - appendix A.3 states that conditional tabular generators [10] and synthetic EHR frameworks [8, 13] can condition generation on available attributes or external summaries, before naming their limitation - but it attributes the capability to the category rather than to CTGAN. The compared baselines are HALO, LSTM, a GPT-style generator, EVA and SynTEG, all EHR-specific; nothing SDV-family is run. Importance 1 under the scale's bottom step for a passing related-work citation; a reviewer reading that fourth mention as prior art the paper departs from would record 2.

summary: Builds a predictor for arithmetic mean roughness in material-extrusion additive manufacturing from process parameters and local surface angle, trained on an 87-run Box-Behnken design, and wraps it in a web tool that renders predicted roughness over an uploaded 3D model so the effect of the staircase effect can be seen before printing. Conditional synthetic augmentation is added with a CGAN the authors build themselves; CTGAN is cited as the tabular conditional-GAN methodology their conditional generation follows, but it is not named in prose and not run.
evidence: the related-work section states that for tabular data, conditional GAN variants have been developed to better capture mixed discrete and continuous variables and complex distributions, citing [13], which is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni (2019); section 3.3 describes the augmenter as a CGAN whose conditioning vector holds the scaled process parameters and the surface-inclination descriptor while the generator emits a roughness value, and states the approach is consistent with tabular CGAN methodologies developed for mixed and multimodal numerical data where conditional generation preserves feature dependencies rather than generating unconditional samples, citing [13] again. The generator is the authors' own; no CTGAN row appears in any results table. MECHANISM NOTE for future curators: do NOT use duplicate_of to resolve two records sharing a url. build.py drops the higher-numbered shard's record as a duplicate url before the retirement pass runs, so a duplicate_of aimed at the surviving record deletes the artifact from the index entirely, and one aimed at the already-dropped record orphans. duplicate_of is for the same artifact appearing under two different urls. title: Diffusion and Flow Matching Models for Tabular Data: A Survey
summary: Surveys diffusion and flow-matching models for tabular data across seven task families - single-table synthesis, multi-relational synthesis, missing-value imputation, trustworthy and privacy-preserving generation, and anomaly detection - setting out a problem definition per family, a taxonomy of design choices over encoding, data-space versus latent-space generation and dependency handling, and comparative analyses of what each group of methods actually isolates. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE prior art the survey departs from: they are named as the earlier methods shown to achieve superior performance before diffusion, their Gaussian-mixture treatment of continuous features and one-hot handling of categoricals are the specific limitations the diffusion case is argued against, and the survey's own statement of the tabular modelling problem takes its notion of a complicated feature distribution from the CTGAN paper.
evidence: section II-A states that VAE-based methods such as TVAE [58] and GOGGLE were shown to achieve superior performance, then that GAN-based methods such as CTGAN [58] have shown promising results for tabular data synthesis but typically use Gaussian mixture models for continuous features, which may be suboptimal for certain real-world data, and handle categorical features with one-hot encoding, substantially increasing dimensionality; section II-B takes the phrase 'complicated distribution' for a tabular feature from [58] in setting out the survey's own problem statement; reference [58] is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni, Modeling tabular data using conditional GAN. Nothing is run - the artifact is a survey. Importance 2 under the convention for prior art a paper departs from. Curation note: this paper was curated in shards 78 and 85 as a duplicate pair and both copies were subsequently removed from main, leaving it in no shard; it is re-curated here. Two prior independent curations both reached citation_only importance 2, which this entry matches.
